findings.where: All running text: the intro paragraph, the Surf, Vibe and What to look for paragraphs, and the coming-soon notice. Worst in the phone notice ('MantaHostels   is   launching   across') and the desktop Vibe paragraph ('Lively  and  social,  leaning').
findings.fault: Body text is fully justified in a narrow column with no hyphenation. The word spacing swings from line to line, so wide gaps and rivers open up and the text reads as stretched and uneven.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker skimming the guide on a phone mid-transit. The uneven gaps break their reading rhythm in exactly the short blocks they scan to decide whether Canggu suits them. The brand promises an effortless, crafted feel, and the stretched lines look unfinished.

findings.fault: 'Vibe' is set in italic, underlined and turquoise. Its sibling headings 'Surf' and 'Good for' are plain ink Quicksand, so one heading out of a set of peers looks like a link. The parts map confirms it does nothing when clicked.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who taps 'Vibe' expecting more detail and gets nothing. A brand reviewer would also object: lagoon-family colour is reserved for links, turquoise is a fill colour and not cleared for text, and peer headings should be set alike.

findings.where: What to look for section heading
findings.fault: This heading is small, uppercase and widely tracked, unlike the large sentence-case Quicksand used for Surf, Vibe and Good for. It is a peer section, but it reads as a lesser label, so the page's heading hierarchy breaks at its most useful section.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker scanning for the practical advice. The section that tells them what to look for in a hostel looks like a caption rather than a section, so it is easy to skip. The brand's casing rule keeps uppercase for badges and filter labels.

findings.fault: The title is in title case. The brand voice is sentence case ('Best hostels in Canggu'), and every other heading on the page follows it.
findings.who_objects: The brand owner, whose voice rule sets sentence case across product copy. The mix of title-case h1 and sentence-case h2s makes the page look assembled from different sources.

findings.fault: Like labels are set in different colours. Some pills carry white text (Long stays, Meeting people, Nightlife, Couples, Solo travellers, Sunsets) and others dark ink (First-time surfers, Remote workers, Yoga, Budget, Cafés, Scooter riders). The text colour seems to follow each pill's fill at random, not any difference in meaning.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning the tags. The white-labelled ones read as selected or more important, which they are not, so a uniform list of traits seems to carry a ranking it doesn't have.
